title: Black Widow
synopsis: An antidote frees Yelena from the Red Room’s control. She turns to Natasha, the older girl who grew up beside her in an undercover household, to help free the other Widows.
verdictRationale: The decisive moment comes after Natasha has the means to defeat her pursuer. She gives Antonia the antidote. Natasha once accepted this girl's death as the price of her own escape. Giving Antonia her freedom makes repentance visible in a way an apology alone could never do.
ageRationale: The sisters describe forced sterilization. A girl is knowingly put in the path of a bombing, and an adult man beats Natasha. Older teens may be better prepared to discuss abuse by people who claim to be family.
reflection: At the dinner table, Yelena has to explain that her childhood mattered even if the adults were acting. Starting with what she remembers, without correcting her feelings, is one way the others can begin to make amends.

title: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
synopsis: An attack on a San Francisco bus sends Shang-Chi to warn his sister. Their father, Wenwu, believes their dead mother is calling him from behind a gate and intends to force it open.
verdictRationale: Shang-Chi risks his safety to warn Xialing and tries to stop his father from endangering a village. The story gives grief and filial love their due, while magic rings, a guardian dragon and creatures that consume souls shape its account of death and power.
ageRationale: A child watches his father take revenge and is trained until his knuckles bleed. The prolonged sight of a creature draining a person's soul may be more frightening than the choreographed fistfights.
reflection: Wenwu once laid down the rings because he wanted to grow old with his wife. After her death, he treats a voice that sounds like hers as permission to endanger others. A family might ask whom we trust enough to hear when grief makes a promise sound irresistible.
